2  NC: 2023:KHC-D:10709  MFA No. 23188 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 22693 of 2012  JUDGMENT MFA No.23188/2012 is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 29.06.2011,
passed by the learned V Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari, in M.V.C. No707/2009, seeking enhancement of compensation whereas MFA No.22693/2012 is filed by the NEKRTC seeking reduction of quantum of compensation.
2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the appellant- claimant and the respondents.
3. The occurrence of accident, injuries sustained by the claimant, coverage of insurance are not in dispute.

4. Learned counsel for NEKRTC submitted that the doctor had stated that the claimant had suffered 30% psychological disability and 25% of physical disability to the whole body but the tribunal has taken 40% as functional disability towards whole body is on higher side.
Further submitted that the compensation granted under NC: 2023:KHC-D:10709 the head injuries pain and suffering is on higher side.
Therefore, prays to reduce the quantum of compensation.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded is on lesser side as lesser percentage of functional disability is taken into consideration.
Therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation.

6. In the present case, from the medical evidence on record it is proved that the claimant had sustained open head injury with depressed frontal bone, frontal lobe contusion and hip joint sublookcession.
The claimant is an agriculturist by profession.
Apart from that CT scan report proves that claimant sustained crack fracture of the body of L-4 vertebrae and undisplaced fracture of femoral head.
The above injuries sustained by the claimant are not disputed.
7. The doctor-PW.2 who is a neurologist who has given disability certificate-Ex.P.52 has deposed that the claimant has severe headache giddiness and suffered NC: 2023:KHC-D:10709 decreased memory.
Also deposed the claimant has suffered left sided weakness and he has MMSE score of 19/30 and grade 4/5 power in the left sided limbs (MMSE- Mini Mental Status Examination).
Therefore, from the evidence of the doctor-PW.2, the brain functions of the claimant are also affected due to the injury sustained in the accident.
It is evidence of doctor-PW.2 that the claimant had suffered 30% psychological disability and 25% of physical disability towards the whole body.
The thing is elicited during course of cross-examination of the doctor proving that the claimant had suffered lesser percentage of disability what he has deposed.

The Tribunal has taken 40% as functional disability is on lower side where it is proved that the claimant has suffered 30%
psychological disability is significant one and as per doctor's evidence, the memory of the claimant is Ajjanna Obaiah S/O T Palaiah vs Mahantesh S/O Veerabhadrappa Goudar on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34304952/
3 decreased.

entities.text: T Palaiah vs Mahantesh S/O Veerabhadrappa Goudar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Also, the MMSE score is 19/30 and grade 4/5 power in the both left legs.
Therefore, the functional disability sustained by the claimant is significant one.
But even though the claimant was doing agriculture work but NC: 2023:KHC-D:10709 certainly cannot be done such work as he was doing before the accident.

Therefore, while considering the psychological disability affected the claimant, the functional disability is taken upon the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another1 as 50% functional disability suffered by the claimant.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In the present case, the claimant was aged 35 years old and he was doing agricultural work.
The accident was caused in the year 2008.
Therefore, as per chart of notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, a sum of Rs.4,250/- per month to be taken as notional monthly income of the claimant.
The Tribunal has not added income towards loss of future prospects in life.

According to the age of the deceased 40% of the income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. (2011) 1 SCC 343 NC: 2023:KHC-D:10709 Pranay Sethi 2 and as per the judgment of the division bench of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company vs. Abdul S/o Mehaboob Tahasildar3 and the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sidram vs.
Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited and another4 i.e. Rs.1,700/-
(Rs.4,250/- of 40%).

sentences.text: The appropriate multiplier applicable as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma & Others vs. Delhi Transport Corpn and Another5 is '16'.

entities.text: Smt.Sarla Verma & Others vs. Delhi Transport Corpn and Another5 is '16'
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss of future earning capacity including loss of future prospects in life' is reassessed and quantified as follows:
Rs.4,250 + 1,700 (40% of Rs.4,250) x 50% x 16 x 12 = Rs.5,71,200/-.
(2017) 16 SCC 680 MFA.No.103807/2016 C/w MFA Nos.103835/2016 &
103807/2018 dated 27.05.2022 2022 ACJ 2611 AIR 2009 SCC 3104 NC:
2023:KHC-D:10709 9.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation under other heads is found to be just, proper and correct which needs no interference.

10. Thus, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads.

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
1. Towards injuries, pain and Rs.1,00,000 suffering.
2. Towards medical expenses Rs.40,000 (As per actual bills and receipts)
3. Towards loss of amenities. Rs.35,000

5. Towards incidental charges like Rs.15,000/-
attendant charges, food, nourishment, conveyance, etc.,.
6. Loss of future earning capacity Rs.5,71,200 including loss of future prospects in life.
Total: Rs.7,74,700 Less: Compensation awarded Rs.4,13,400 by tribunal:
Enhanced compensation: Rs.3,61,300 NC: 2023:KHC-D:10709 11.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,74,700/- as against what has been awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
The NEKRTC is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

12. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) MFA No.23188/2012 filed by the claimant is allowed in part.
ii) MFA No.22693/2012 filed by the NEKRTC is dismissed.
iii) The judgment and award dated 29.06.2011, passed by the learned V Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari, in MVC No707/2009, stands modified.
